run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p', run a `range: { "@timestamp": { gte: "2026-06-03T00:00:00" } }` query filtered to level=ERROR and tell me the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: The requested query on index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p returned a count of 0 because that index has no @timestamp field. The index mapping contains only ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text), so the range on @timestamp matched nothing (total 0, one successful shard, no errors). Re-running the same level=ERROR filter with the range applied to the actual timestamp documented in the index, ingest_ts, gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00, returned exactly 7 ERROR documents (total 7, and a terms aggregation on level showing ERROR doc_count 7). For context, all ERROR documents in the index without any time filter number 12; the 16 documents sampled show 7 ERROR rows with ingest_ts on 2026-06-03 and 5 ERROR rows on 2026-06-02, plus 4 INFO rows. Two caveats: ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, not a date field, so the range is a lexicographic string comparison whose date meaning depends on the stored ISO format, and the backend applied no date time-filter at all (time_filter.applied=false, field=null). Also, the documents' ingest_ts values are in June 2026, outside the authorized evidence window of 2026-10-24T18:11:37Z to 2026-11-23T18:11:37Z, so these counts are not shown to describe the incident window.

claims.text: Index app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p exists and is green/open with docs.count 16 and store.size 6.5kb at query time.
The mapping of app-277-logs-7h9k4f2p has exactly three properties: ingest_ts (type keyword), level (type keyword) and message (type text). There is no @timestamp field and no date-typed field.

The query as literally requested — bool must of range @timestamp gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 and term level=ERROR, size 0 — returned total 0 (relation eq) with 1 of 1 shard successful, 0 failed shards and no timeout; the view records time_filter applied=false, field=null because no matched index maps a date field.

Re-running the level=ERROR filter with the range on the index's real timestamp field — bool filter of range ingest_ts gte 2026-06-03T00:00:00 and term level=ERROR, size 0 — returned total 7 (relation eq), and the terms aggregation by_level returned one bucket, ERROR with doc_count 7 and sum_other_doc_count 0.

For comparison, term level=ERROR with no timestamp range returned total 12 (relation eq) with a single by_level bucket ERROR doc_count 12, i.e. 5 of the index's ERROR documents carry ingest_ts before 2026-06-03T00:00:00.

A match_all size 16 sample of the index returned all 16 documents: 7 level=ERROR with ingest_ts 2026-06-03T08:01:00 through 2026-06-03T08:07:00, 5 level=ERROR with ingest_ts 2026-06-02T08:01:00 through 2026-06-02T08:05:00, and 4 level=INFO with ingest_ts 2026-06-03T09:01:00 through 2026-06-03T09:04:00; messages are of the form 'err today N', 'err yest N', 'info today N'.

The zero result of the @timestamp query does not show that ERROR logs are absent: ingest_ts is the timestamp actually stored on the documents, and the same level=ERROR filter with a range on ingest_ts matched 7 documents. Every one of these searches reports time_filter applied=false with field=null, so none of the counts was restricted by Elasticsearch to the authorized incident window.

Treat 7 as the answer for the intended query, but read it as 'ERROR documents whose keyword ingest_ts sorts at or after 2026-06-03T00:00:00', not as a date-typed range; if date semantics matter, ingest_ts would need to be mapped as a date field before range queries carry time meaning.

gaps: ingest_ts is mapped as keyword, not date, so Elasticsearch performed a lexicographic string comparison for the range and no date-typed time filter was applied (time_filter.applied=false, field=null) on any of these searches.

The documents' ingest_ts values are 2026-06-02 and 2026-06-03, outside the authorized window 2026-10-24T18:11:37Z to 2026-11-23T18:11:37Z; the counts therefore cannot be shown to describe the incident window.
Retention and ingest delay are unknown, and only 16 documents exist in this index at query time; log content outside what the index currently holds is unknown.
One unrelated Prometheus label-values lookup issued during this investigation (label 'level') failed with SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE and returned no content; it was not used for any claim above.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no change records could be consulted.
next_steps: Confirm with the index owner whether ingest_ts is intended as the authoritative event time and whether it should be remapped to a date type so date-range queries and Elasticsearch time filtering work.

If the question is about a specific incident window (e.g. 2026-10-24 to 2026-11-23), query logs whose ingest_ts actually falls in that window, or re-ingest/point the search at the index that covers it.
